subject: Re: Lyrion capacity ask — peak profile & safety-lane sizing
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@lyrion.ai>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@lyrion.ai
Date: 2027-09-29T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Lyrion commitment: capacity ask and SLO targets

Camila — thanks for taking this. We’re finalizing internal commitment numbers and need a quick sizing sketch to include in the MOU. High-level asks:

- Target SLOs: p95 <= 300ms for text-completion flows; p99 <= 550ms.
- Expected steady-state: ~60 requests/sec (r/s) during business hours.
- Average tokens per request: ~120 tokens (most responses 60-180 tokens).
- Peak shaping: expected 11:00–13:00 local time spikes up to ~3x steady-state for short windows (10–20min).
- Desired safety/headroom: vendor guidance for minimum 1.5x above peak.

Attached: initial SLA draft and a small 48h traffic sample (lyrion_traffic_sample.csv). Can you provide a quick tokens/sec estimate and guidance on how many A100-equivalent GPUs we should reserve under a dedicated slab? Also, any recommendations on fallback/quantization if we need to hit the p99 numbers under heavy bursts?

Thanks — Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Product
Lyrion.ai

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@lyrion.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-29T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lyrion capacity ask and SLO targets

Samira — quick sketch below based on the numbers in your CSV and the SLA targets. This is a conservative starting point; we’ll refine after we see the per-minute histograms.

Summary estimates (raw):
- Baseline tokens/sec = steady_rps * avg_tokens = 60 r/s * 120 tok = 7,200 tokens/sec.
- Peak shaping (3x for short windows) => instantaneous peak = 21,600 tokens/sec.
- 1.5x safety factor over instantaneous peak => planning target = ~32,400 tokens/sec.

Redwood mapping assumptions:
- Model: redwood-2L-13B (8-bit quant / optimized kernels) — typical production throughput on A100-class hardware: ~25k tokens/sec per GPU sustained for mixed-length payloads with our continuous batching profile.
- KV/prefix caching not applied: numbers above are raw. With prefix caching we commonly see an effective tokens reduction of ~12–18% depending on reuse.

Sizing guidance (conservative):
- Minimum reserved slab: 2x A100-equivalent GPUs (sustained capacity ~50k tok/s) — would meet plan but leaves limited headroom on sustained peaks.
- Recommended reserved slab: 3x A100-equivalent GPUs — sustained 75k tok/s, gives ~2.3x headroom vs steady-state and ~2.6x vs instantaneous peak after 1.5x safety, making it resilient to sustained high-traffic periods and allowing for rolling restarts.
- Burst buffer: enable short-term burst capacity (ephemeral / autoscale) to cover multi-queue spikes beyond 20 minutes.

Latency notes vs SLOs:
- With 3 GPUs and standard batching (100–150ms batching latency budget) we expect p95 around 180–260ms for the profile you sent. p99 will depend on tail events and queuing; with a 3-GPU slab and burst buffer p99 should be ~450–550ms which aligns with your target but we’ll measure during canary.

Fallbacks to improve p99 during spikes:
- Quantized model variant (4-bit) can increase throughput ~1.6x, reducing GPU count for short-term demand but may change output distribution — we recommend a small eval set (we can run A/B) before enabling.
- Lightweight fallback (e.g., redwood-2L-6B) for best-effort responses under extreme load; keep routing rules to prefer fidelity first.

Next steps:
1) If you confirm willingness to reserve 3 GPUs, we’ll produce a formal capacity plan + cost delta for committed vs baseline.
2) Karhtik will run a short simulation (with and without prefix caching and with 4-bit quant) and return updated GPU counts and latency curves.
3) We’ll schedule a 30m canary run to validate p95/p99 under representative traffic.

—Camila
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, Samira Khan <samira.khan@lyrion.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-29T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lyrion capacity ask — simulation & optimizations

Looping in a slightly more detailed run of the numbers and two optimization levers we can apply. I modeled three scenarios using the CSV: conservative (no caching, 8-bit), optimized-caching (prefix KV applied), and quantized (4-bit).

Scenario A — conservative (no caching, 8-bit)- Tokens/sec demand (planning target) = 32.4k tok/s -> GPUs required = ceil(32.4k / 25k) = 2 GPUs (but we recommend 3 to cover background ops + maintenance).

Scenario B — with prefix caching (~15% effective token reduction):- Adjusted peak demand = 32.4k * 0.85 ~= 27.5k -> GPUs required = 2 (25k each) but headroom drops; 2 GPUs OK with aggressive burst buffer for short windows.

Scenario C — 4-bit quantized variant (1.6x throughput uplift):- Effective tokens per GPU = 25k * 1.6 = 40k tok/s -> Planning target 32.4k comfortably served on 1 GPU from a pure throughput standpoint, but latency and model fidelity tradeoffs apply. For SLOs, we still prefer at least 2 GPUs in a production slab for redundancy and to keep p99 bounded.

Latency modeling notes:
- Batching parameters matter: lower batch windows reduce p95 but raise cost. For your p95 target of 300ms, keep batching windows small (~80–120ms) and leverage NVLink-style pooling for KV.
- Cold-starts: warmup policies (reserve warm KV cache) reduce first-request p99 by ~300–400ms during spikes. Plan for a warmup budget in the SLA.

Recommendation (practical):
- Commit: 2x A100-equivalent GPUs as the base Dedicated slab, paired with a 1 GPU reserved burst buffer (ephemeral) for short-duration peaks.
- Enable prefix caching by default (we can tune threshold) and plan an optional canary to measure quality impact if you enable 4-bit quant.
- SLA language: include a warmup window of 10 minutes for sustained bursts >2x baseline and an agreed traffic histogram requirement to trigger autoscale credits.

I’ll attach the simulation sheet and a quick latency curve snapshot.

Attachment: lyrion_peak_profile.xlsx (xlsx)

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Samira / Team — quick summary and clear action items so we can fold this into the commercial proposal and MOU.

Summary decisions:
- Commercial ask we’ll size for: base Dedicated slab = 2x A100-equivalent GPUs (committed), plus a 1x ephemeral GPU buffer for short bursts (autoscale).
- Ops/config: enable prefix KV caching; keep 4-bit quantization as opt-in (canary run required).
- Latency expectation: p95 ~200–300ms (target), p99 ~450–550ms (target) once canary validated.

Deliverables & timeline:
1) Lyrion provides: per-minute traffic histogram for last 7 days (CSV) + representative prompt set (we’ll run evaluation). Deadline: EOW.
2) Redwood provides: final capacity sizing sheet + cost delta (committed 2-GPU vs 3-GPU conservative) and an MOA clause for warmup/autoscale credits. ETA: 3 business days after data receipt.
3) Schedule: 30m canary run (we’ll propose times after sizing is finalized).

Attachments referenced: lyrion_peak_profile.xlsx, draft SLA (lyrion_sla_draft.pdf). Please send the 7-day histogram and confirm whether procurement needs a DocuSign ready SLA or a redline first.
